name: α1A
description: Gq-coupled excitatory NA receptor; modulates cortical, hippocampal and brainstem excitability.

name: α1B
description: Gq-coupled excitatory NA receptor; postsynaptic, widely expressed across cortex and subcortex.

name: α1D
description: Gq-coupled excitatory NA receptor; postsynaptic, in cortex, hippocampus and brainstem.

name: α2A
description: Gi-coupled inhibitory NA receptor; presynaptic autoreceptor in locus coeruleus, postsynaptic in prefrontal cortex.

name: α2B
description: Gi-coupled inhibitory NA receptor; limited CNS expression in thalamus, hippocampus and cerebellar Purkinje cells.

name: α2C
description: Gi-coupled inhibitory NA receptor; widespread in basal ganglia, amygdala, hippocampus, cortex and midbrain.

name: β1
description: Gs-coupled excitatory NA receptor; in cortex, cingulate and accumbens; modulates fear and circadian timing.

name: β2
description: Gs-coupled excitatory NA receptor; in cerebellum, cortex and hippocampus.

name: M1
description: Gq postsynaptic muscarinic receptor; slow EPSP, drives cortical/hippocampal cognition and memory.

name: M2
description: Gi-coupled presynaptic autoreceptor; restrains acetylcholine release (also slows the heart).

name: M3
description: Gq postsynaptic muscarinic receptor; acts in hypothalamus and brainstem autonomic centres.

name: M4
description: Gi-coupled receptor enriched in striatum; presynaptic autoreceptor that brakes D1 dopamine drive.

name: M5
description: Gq receptor on substantia nigra/VTA dopamine neurons; facilitates dopamine release.

name: Neuronal α4β2 nAChR
description: High-affinity nicotine receptor; cation channel on dopamine terminals, drives nicotine addiction.

name: Neuronal α7 nAChR
description: Homomeric Ca2+-permeable cation channel; α-bungarotoxin-sensitive, implicated in schizophrenia.

name: D1
description: Most abundant dopamine receptor; Gs-coupled, excitatory; drives the striatal direct pathway.

name: D2
description: Gi-coupled, inhibitory; drives the indirect pathway and acts as a presynaptic autoreceptor; antipsychotic target.

name: D3
description: D2-like, Gi-coupled, inhibitory; concentrated in limbic ventral striatum, highest dopamine affinity.

name: D4
description: D2-like, Gi-coupled, inhibitory; enriched in frontal cortex; linked to attention and ADHD.

name: D5
description: D1-like, Gs-coupled, excitatory; low-abundance but widespread; high constitutive activity, prominent in hippocampus.

name: GABA-A
description: Ubiquitous Cl- channel; target of benzodiazepines, alcohol, anaesthetics, neurosteroids; anxiety/epilepsy/insomnia.

name: GABA-B
description: Widespread Gi/o GPCR; opens K+ channels, curbs Ca2+ and transmitter release; baclofen target.

name: NMDA
description: Coincidence-detecting Ca2+ channel driving LTP/memory; ketamine/memantine target, schizophrenia hypofunction.

name: AMPA
description: Fast cation channel mediating most fast excitatory transmission; its trafficking underlies synaptic plasticity.

name: Kainate
description: Cation channel with more limited distribution; postsynaptic excitation plus presynaptic modulation of release.

name: mGluR1
description: Group I Gq receptor; postsynaptic excitation, potentiates NMDA currents; strong in cerebellar Purkinje cells.

name: mGluR2
description: Group II Gi presynaptic autoreceptor lowering glutamate release; agonists target anxiety and schizophrenia.

name: mGluR3
description: Group II Gi receptor on terminals and glia reducing glutamate release; neuroprotective, schizophrenia interest.

name: mGluR4
description: Group III Gi presynaptic receptor suppressing release; basal-ganglia activation proposed for Parkinson's.

name: mGluR5
description: Group I Gq receptor potentiating NMDA; fragile-X and psychiatric drug target, dense in striatum/cortex.

name: mGluR7
description: Group III Gi presynaptic autoreceptor, the most widespread mGluR, gating release at active zones; lowest affinity.

name: Glycine
description: Ionotropic Cl- channel; major inhibitory receptor of the brainstem (its dominant spinal-cord site is out of frame).

name: H1
description: Gq excitatory; drives wakefulness and arousal; its blockade by antihistamines causes sedation.

name: H2
description: Gs cAMP receptor; mainly gastric, with a lighter CNS role in basal ganglia and cortex.

name: H3
description: Gi presynaptic auto/heteroreceptor; CNS-wide; curbs transmitter release; cognition and wakefulness target.

name: μ (MOR)
description: Main analgesia/euphoria/dependence opioid receptor; dense in PAG, thalamus, striatum, amygdala.

name: δ (DOR)
description: Opioid receptor modulating mood and anxiety; cortex, striatum, amygdala, olfactory bulb.

name: κ (KOR)
description: Opioid receptor driving dysphoria and stress; striatum, claustrum, hypothalamus, PAG.

name: 5-HT1A
description: Gi-coupled; raphe somatodendritic autoreceptor and postsynaptic; anxiety/depression target (buspirone, SSRIs).

name: 5-HT1B
description: Gi-coupled; presynaptic terminal autoreceptor in basal ganglia; triptan target for migraine.

name: 5-HT1D
description: Gi-coupled; low-level basal ganglia/cortex; presynaptic terminal autoreceptor; triptan migraine target.

name: 5-HT1E
description: Gi-coupled; frontal cortex, hippocampus and olfactory bulb; implicated in human memory; poorly characterized.

name: 5-HT1F
description: Gi-coupled; cortex, thalamus, subthalamus; target of lasmiditan for migraine without vasoconstriction.

name: 5-HT2A
description: Gq-coupled; dense on cortical pyramidal cells; mediates psychedelics; atypical antipsychotic target.

name: 5-HT2B
description: Gq-coupled; presynaptic autoreceptor on raphe 5-HT neurons; also peripheral (cardiac valves, valvulopathy risk); sparse CNS in hypothalamus, cortex, amygdala.

name: 5-HT2C
description: Gq-coupled; choroid plexus, cortex, limbic and hypothalamus; regulates appetite and mood (lorcaserin).

name: 5-HT3
description: Ionotropic cation channel; area postrema drives nausea/vomiting; antiemetic target (ondansetron).

name: 5-HT4
description: Gs-coupled; hippocampus, striatum, cortex; cognition and gut motility.

name: 5-HT5A
description: Gi-coupled; cortex, cerebellum, hippocampus, hypothalamus; least understood subtype, possible circadian role.

name: 5-HT6
description: Gs-coupled; striatum, cortex, hippocampus; almost entirely CNS; cognition target.

name: 5-HT7
description: Gs-coupled; thalamus, hypothalamus, hippocampus; circadian rhythm, mood and thermoregulation.

name: CB1
description: Gi GPCR; presynaptic retrograde signaling, THC target; one of the most abundant brain GPCRs.

name: A2A
description: Gs GPCR concentrated in striatum on D2 indirect-pathway neurons; caffeine antagonist target.

name: σ1
description: Intracellular ER chaperone (not a classic channel/GPCR); fluvoxamine acts partly via it.

name: MT1
description: Gi GPCR in hypothalamic SCN + pituitary pars tuberalis; sleep/circadian, ramelteon target.

name: MT2
description: Gi GPCR in hypothalamic SCN; drives circadian phase-shifting.
